SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
The patient reports onset of low back pain on 05/03/2026. She describes diffuse lumbar discomfort without radiculopathy.
Exam: Inspection shows normal lumbar range of motion; palpation reveals paraspinal tenderness. Neurologic exam demonstrates normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation. She denies any red flags including trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel symptoms, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit.
Assessment: Acute low back pain, likely musculoskeletal.
Plan: Start NSAIDs today (ibuprofen 600 mg q6h PRN). Refer to physical therapy for core strengthening and lumbar stabilization, aiming for 12 sessions over 6 weeks. Follow up in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient returns for physical therapy check-in. Low back pain persists despite treatment.
Exam: Similar to prior; mild paraspinal tenderness; neurologic exam unchanged, normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, sensation.
Assessment: Ongoing low back pain after conservative measures.
Plan: Document completion of conservative therapy. NSAIDs were started on 05/04/2026 and continued until 06/18/2026 with partial relief. Physical therapy was initiated on 05/07/2026, consisting of 12 sessions, and concluded on 06/18/2026 without improvement. No further PT authorized at this time. Consider advanced imaging.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient reports continued low back pain after completing NSAIDs and physical therapy. No new symptoms.
Exam: Stable; neurologic exam normal; no red flags.
Assessment: Persistent low back pain unresponsive to NSAIDs and a full course of physical therapy.
Plan: Since conservative therapy has failed, order lumbar MRI to evaluate for structural pathology. If MRI shows significant findings, spine surgery referral will be considered.

HPI: Patient returns for results discussion; MRI ordered previously.
Exam: Unchanged; neurologic exam normal.
Assessment: Awaiting lumbar MRI results.
Plan: Order lumbar spine MRI without contrast today. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings.
